steps.name: Siege
steps.text: These statues...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: They're the kings of Victoria.
Phantoms roam here.
Not the spirits of the dead... but a shadow of history and memory.
Their voices have become clear.
They are familiar and warm, as though they came from a forgotten corner of her memory.
Just like how her name was called with scolding and love when she lingered too long in the garden.
Just like how her name was called with anxiety and urging when she sneaked out of the palace to see what was outside with curious eyes.
Just like how her name was called with pride and approval when she swung her little wooden sword, dreaming about becoming a warrior without equal.
But...
Who is calling her like this?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: The statues of the Aslan and Draco kings are displayed here.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Here is your grandfather, Frederick III, Conqueror of Gaul. By his side is his mother, Elizabeth the Glorious.
All in the procession begin treading lightly.
She is searching. She knows it is fruitless, but her eyes cannot help but search.
She stops before one of the statues.
It was never finished, leaving behind only a rough silhouette.
Chisel marks can be clearly seen, and an elaborate robe has yet to be liberated from the stone.
Where the face should be, there is only a blur of rock with the slight hint of eyes.
The crown on the head hints at the statue's position.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: By tradition, Originium Arts is not used in the creation of these statues. They are the result of years of hard work by royal sculptors.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: His Majesty's passing was... sudden.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...I know.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: His Majesty's burden was heavy, politically and tangibly.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: The empire was saddled with war debts, and the declining Draco hardly welcomed continued Aslan rule with open arms.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: No matter how others might assess His Majesty, Father and I did not feel that he was inferior in any way to the kings who lie here.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Perhaps, Allerdale.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I don't remember.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Maybe that's how he looked in my memories.
Was it him calling? Or all of them?
The statues do not look the same. Some of them look solemn, others look kind.
She finds no image of them in her memory, but feels some kind of connection with them, deep down.
The only ones who may style themselves Victoria are the monarchs of Victoria, and the heir to the throne.
Therefore, she is Victoria, just like them.
She looks away.
Compared to vast and glorious Victoria, she is more familiar with the tiny taverns of Norport Borough, the scalding bitterness of cheap ale, and licking a sour lollipop after a fight.
She turns away.
In that moment, she spots a shadow behind the statues.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: To arms!
They all grab their weapons.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Looks like we found the ones who left the traces.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Sarkaz bodies.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Hundreds, if not more.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Most have decomposed into skeletons, but their clothes tell us they were Sarkaz Royal Court elites, and Confessarius guards.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Frankly, the word 'elite' is an understatement. A fight with any one of them would be a desperate struggle.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Who were they fighting?
She feels Allerdale's breath grow heavy.
Bronze continues to glitter in the shadows of the corpses.
Even history could not rob them of their color.
She keeps moving forward.
The knights of the empire never back down.
One after another.
Swords, fire, corrosive Arts. An entire suit of armor is covered in dried blood.
Arts-imbued pila over five meters in length impaled their torsos.
They kept formation, they fought on.
Nothing could defeat them. Not the Royal Court, not the Confessarii.
Not even death.
Suddenly, she understands.
She understands why the sound of steam has not been heard in Londinium for the past four years.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Steam Knights...
Allerdale stumbles. Siege extends an arm to hold her friend..

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Are you alright?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'm fine. It's just the air.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I think back to the steam armor of Cumberland Manor.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: They were always defending, no matter the cost.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: They were... Steam Knights.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: They carried the glorious banner of Victoria.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No.

a.text: Is it the sound of steam gushing when the knights charge?
What is this emotion, so potent that it threatens to break through everything?
She closes her eyes. The emotions confuse her, but the conclusion is clear.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: They...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: They were betrayed.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's clear from the layout of the bodies that the Steam Knights were the attackers, and the Sarkaz were the defenders.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Ridiculous, isn't it?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: This isn't a story of how the Steam Knights defended the symbol of Victoria to their last breaths, in the face of an overwhelming Sarkaz tide.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It was a trap.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The knights stumbled into an ambush that the Sarkaz prepared for them.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: An ambush that the Sarkaz set in the Mausoleum of Kings.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Sacrilege!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: How did the Sarkaz get in here? The key to the Mausoleum of Kings is only...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: No...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We handed it over to them.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The traitor, Duke Cavendish? Or the clown, Duke Stafford?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: No Steam Knight has been seen for four years. They were all here.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: One or two dukes blinded by ambition could not recall all the Steam Knights to Londinium.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: They were betrayed—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: By all of Victoria.
The burning palace, the golden mane.
She could not shake the images ever since she set foot within.
She hears the angry roaring of a man, plots being whispered in the shadows.
She hears laments and curses.
Frenzied cries, fateful announcements.
Roaring, scolding, sobbing, sneering.
She hears—
Drip.
The sound of tears falling.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Siege...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: These Steam Knights...
Dagda tries her best to suppress her sobbing. The girl who calls herself a knight has never cried, no matter how desperate the situation is.
But now, tears are flowing down her face.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I don't understand... I don't understand... why...
Siege walks up to her and puts her arms around her trembling shoulders.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm sorry, Dagda, I was wrong.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Victoria is more than just Parliament and the nobility. It's you and me as well.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: There are still people willing to cry for them.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We don't have too much time.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But if I'm still king to you, then let me give an order, just this once.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Dagda, Knight of the Tower.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Salute these men, who held their glorious banner high even after they were betrayed.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Salute them as a knight would, on our behalf.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Thirty, thirty-one, thirty-two...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: So many suits of armor...

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: They all died here.
Her gaze sweeps over each and every suit of unmoving armor.
She salutes them one by one.
Even though those within died years ago, even though she is holding a strange metal claw rather than a ceremonial sword, she performs the proper rites in accordance with tradition.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You're a knight too.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: ...I was.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I used to be a knight of Victoria... just like them.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: A Knight of the Tower...

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Many see it as no more than a noble title.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Yes. We've had no one left to defend, ever since His Majesty left us.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Silly, isn't it? A bunch of pompous knights, guarding an empty palace.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: All of us, as we stood upon the tower, knew that the palace behind us was empty. We would only see lights coming from the city in front of us.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: I heard you're the heir to somebody important.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: But it sounds like being a Knight of the Tower isn't a particularly attractive job.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: My mother was the Countess of Manchester.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But all my family has left is a lonely manor in a border city.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Your mother loved you. She left you with a backup plan.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: She thought that you would be safe with the Knights of the Tower, without a king to protect.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: My master told me that a king would return, and the Knights of the Tower would wipe away their shame.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Until the Sarkaz army smashed open the doors of the tower with their weapons.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: The Sarkaz didn't do anything to the palace, at least not openly. They didn't want to give anyone excuses.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: But they couldn't tolerate the existence of the Knights of the Tower.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: We tried.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: The bulk of the Knights of the Tower went with His Majesty. All that was left was a few master knights, and a bunch of self-exiled pariahs.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But we tried!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: We'd brought shame upon ourselves once. We couldn't do it again.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You weren't born when the old Lion King was hanged.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Don't put this burden on yourself.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: But I swore an oath! I was one of them, even without the king's blessing!

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: They tricked me... They decided that I was to live, before they made their final charge.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Master Finn was seriously injured when he sent me out of the tower. I could see blood seeping from under his armor.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: I'd never seen such an expression on his face... he said it was liberation.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: He said it was an end to regret and guilt, an end to long years of ignoble existence.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: He never asked what I wanted! I wanted to die with them!

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Life can't be so easily thrown away.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Dying is simple. All it takes is one bolt, one thrust of a blade, one infected wound, one tiny little piece of active Originium.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Living is hard. Living is a constant struggle against the feeling that dying is a way out.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: You've walked a long road and made good friends. You didn't let your elders down. You did well.
The veteran mercenary pats Dagda's shoulders.
It's the touch of a stranger, but it reminds her of the warmth of her long-dead comrades, how their palms gently touched her head and shoulders like this, time and again.
She never had the chance to mourn them, all those years away from Londinium.
The war is not over. It is not yet time to reminisce.
But as she gazes upon the broken armor of the Steam Knights, all the memories of the last battle of the Knights of the Tower gush to the surface.
She does not understand. Why is the end always like this, when there are so many people who love this land?
Why must heroes fade away quietly in the dark? Why are they never triumphant?
She can't take it anymore.

steps.name: Totter
steps.text: Cry if you need to. The others can't see with me standing here.
The suits of armor remain silent around them.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You look nervous, Allerdale.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: ...Do I?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I wonder... how do you feel about the Steam Knights?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: They couldn't stop what happened twenty-six years ago.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I don't know, and I don't really care.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: But someone by the name of Gawain told me that there were no Steam Knights in Londinium at the time.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Parliament sent them away.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: But they did nothing when they returned.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: What do you think, then, Allerdale?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I can tell you really revere the Steam Knights.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Revere? I don't know if I can say that.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'm just thinking... Sir Charles Lynch was the last Steam Knight to be knighted during His Majesty's reign.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: There were no new Steam Knights in the two decades following.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Was it a warning? Or the price of a struggle that no one knows about? Did the dukes have their blades pointed at each other's throats?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Perhaps the betrayal had already started by then.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I can't imagine what kind of slow death it must have been.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Victoria killed itself.
The voices mutter in protest.
Siege pretends not to hear, and repeats calmly, but strongly.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Victoria killed itself with its own greed, ambition and desire.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Will you wipe the slate clean, Your Royal Highness Alexandrina?
The voices fall silent. They are waiting for an answer too.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'll do what I must.
